Description: External application weakness or exposed management service can provide a path into enterprise systems.
Tactic Sequence: Initial Access → Execution → Discovery → Lateral Movement
Assessment Focus: External exposure, application/configuration review, segmentation, authentication, logging, safe validation.
Expected Evidence: Internet exposure inventory; architecture; auth evidence; logs; validated observations.
Potential Impact: Credential compromise, enterprise access, data exposure, potential path toward OT.

Attack Path: Public remote access to internal network
Typical Path: Remote Access & Third Parties → Corporate IT / OT
Description: Externally reachable VPN, remote desktop gateway, bastion or vendor access may provide a path to internal resources.
Assessment Focus: Review exposure, MFA, device trust, authorization, routing, segmentation and monitoring.
Safety Mode: Controlled; OT access path must be explicitly approved.
Expected Evidence: VPN config, access logs, MFA evidence, routes, ACLs, session records.

Attack Path: Compromised identity to privileged enterprise access
Description: A weak, overprivileged, dormant, shared or compromised account can enable broad access.
Tactic Sequence: Initial Access → Privilege Escalation → Discovery → Lateral Movement
Assessment Focus: Review lifecycle, MFA, privilege boundaries, service accounts, PAM, break-glass and logging.
Expected Evidence: IAM exports, group memberships, MFA/PAM settings, audit logs.
Potential Impact: Unauthorized privileged access and downstream compromise.

Description: Targeted social engineering may obtain credentials or cause execution.
Assessment Focus: Assess awareness and controls using approved simulations; never harvest real credentials without explicit authorization.
Expected Evidence: Campaign authorization, results, mail controls, user/reporting metrics.
Potential Impact: Account compromise and subsequent lateral movement.

Typical Path: Remote Access & Third Parties → OT / ICS
Description: Vendor support channels can create trusted paths into plant environments.
Tactic Sequence: Initial Access → Lateral Movement → Process Impact
Assessment Focus: Review vendor accounts, time-bound access, jump hosts, approvals, monitoring, segmentation and session controls.
Expected Evidence: Vendor inventory, contracts, access logs, routes, jump-host records.
Potential Impact: Unauthorized OT access, process manipulation, persistence.

Description: Insufficient segmentation or permissive conduits can allow movement from business systems into OT.
Assessment Focus: Map zones/conduits, firewall policy, allowed flows, remote services and monitoring.
Safety Mode: Passive/read-only unless ROE explicitly permits controlled validation.
Expected Evidence: Network diagrams, firewall rules, flow records, packet metadata.

Description: Shared accounts, dual-homed hosts, gateways or data services may provide reverse movement.
Assessment Focus: Assess dual-homing, trust, routing, authentication and data exchange boundaries.
Expected Evidence: Routing, host configs, service relationships, logs.

Description: Compromise of engineering workstations can expose controller projects, credentials and programming functions.
Assessment Focus: Review engineering workstation hardening, project integrity, removable media, privileges, controller access and change control.
Safety Mode: No live program changes; lab/digital twin for validation.
Expected Evidence: Project hashes, access logs, engineering configs, change records.
Potential Impact: PLC/DCS manipulation, IP theft, unsafe process change.

Description: Malicious or unauthorized engineering project changes can reach controllers through approved engineering workflows.
Assessment Focus: Assess project signing/integrity, repository controls, approval workflow, offline backups and download restrictions.
Safety Mode: Do not download altered programs to production.
Expected Evidence: Project integrity evidence, approvals, hashes, backup status.

Description: Weakly secured historians, gateways or protocol translators may expose control networks.
Assessment Focus: Assess routing, protocol exposure, authentication, read/write permissions and monitoring.
Expected Evidence: Flow captures, ACLs, gateway configs, protocol inventory.
Potential Impact: Unauthorized commands or loss of visibility.

Description: Unauthenticated or weakly protected industrial protocols may permit unauthorized messaging if network access is obtained.
Assessment Focus: Review protocol security, trust boundaries, command/reporting paths, allowlists and monitoring; use lab for active message validation.
Expected Evidence: Protocol inventory, packet metadata/captures, ACLs, control documentation.

Description: Access to control servers/controllers can expose program, parameter, mode or I/O manipulation opportunities.
Assessment Focus: Review access control, engineering paths, change control, backups and monitoring.
Safety Mode: Production-safe; use lab/digital twin for changes.
Expected Evidence: Controller config, project backup, change logs, access logs.
Potential Impact: Loss of control, production impact, safety impact.

Attack Path: HMI compromise to loss of view/control
Description: HMI compromise can affect operator visibility or access to control functions.
Assessment Focus: Review HMI hardening, least privilege, session controls, application allowlisting and monitoring.
Expected Evidence: HMI config, sessions, logs, screen evidence.
Potential Impact: Loss of view/control and delayed response.

Description: Application server weaknesses can expose control functions and process data.
Tactic Sequence: Initial Access → Execution → Discovery → Process Control
Assessment Focus: Assess application services, APIs, authentication, patching, segmentation and monitoring.
Expected Evidence: App configs, API evidence, service inventory, logs.

Description: Weak separation between basic control and safety/protection systems can increase consequence potential.
Assessment Focus: Review SIS/Safety PLC architecture, independence, access, engineering controls, monitoring and change governance.
Safety Mode: Safety systems are never actively manipulated in production for routine VAPT.
Expected Evidence: Architecture, access lists, safety lifecycle evidence, logs, approvals.

Description: Weak industrial/corporate wireless controls may expose plant segments or field devices.
Assessment Focus: Assess segmentation, authentication, encryption, rogue device controls and monitoring.
Expected Evidence: Wireless config, auth evidence, RF inventory, network mapping.

Description: USB/removable media can bridge isolated environments.
Assessment Focus: Assess media control, scanning, allowlisting, kiosk/process, transient asset governance and logs.
Safety Mode: Use test media only under approved procedure.
Expected Evidence: Media policy, logs, endpoint controls, approval records.

Description: Cloud services, edge gateways or private connectivity can create a path toward plant resources.
Assessment Focus: Review IAM, private connectivity, API permissions, routing, gateways and segmentation.
Expected Evidence: Cloud IAM, route tables, security groups, API logs, architecture.

Attack Path: Cloud storage/data exposure to IP theft
Description: Misconfigured object storage, databases or APIs can expose sensitive manufacturing data.
Assessment Focus: Review access policy, encryption, public exposure, secrets, logging and retention.
Expected Evidence: IAM/policy evidence, access logs, object ACLs, classification.
Potential Impact: IP, PII, production and commercial data exposure.

Description: Compromise of business/manufacturing applications or integrations may alter production, quality, inventory or scheduling data.
Assessment Focus: Review application/API authorization, service accounts, data integrity, segregation and interface controls.
Expected Evidence: API logs, role matrices, interface configs, transaction evidence.

Description: Weak API authorization or integration trust can enable unauthorized data or actions across systems.
Assessment Focus: Assess authN/authZ, scopes, mTLS/signatures where applicable, replay protection, rate controls and logging.
Expected Evidence: Requests/responses, API specs, auth policies, logs.

Description: Compromise of source, build, dependency, artifact or signing workflows can propagate to deployed systems.
Assessment Focus: Review source protection, CI/CD identity, dependency controls, SBOM, signing, artifact integrity and approvals.
Safety Mode: No malicious artifact deployment to production.
Expected Evidence: Pipeline logs, SBOM, signatures, repo permissions, artifact hashes.

Description: Compromised update mechanisms or unsigned/unverified firmware can affect industrial devices.
Assessment Focus: Review update provenance, signing, validation, rollback, maintenance windows and vendor controls.
Safety Mode: No firmware alteration on production devices.
Expected Evidence: Firmware hashes/signatures, update records, vendor evidence.

Description: Attackers may target backups to reduce recovery capability before disruption.
Assessment Focus: Review isolation, immutability, credentials, retention, restore testing and monitoring.
Safety Mode: Do not delete/alter production backups during VAPT.
Expected Evidence: Backup configs, immutability evidence, restore tests, access logs.

Attack Path: Ransomware from IT to manufacturing operations
Description: A corporate compromise may affect production-supporting systems, shared services and recovery capabilities.
Assessment Focus: Assess segmentation, privileged access, EDR, backup resilience, application dependencies and response.
Safety Mode: Validate through tabletop/lab unless explicit safe simulation.
Expected Evidence: Network paths, EDR controls, backup evidence, IR records.

Description: Unauthorized physical access can enable direct interaction with devices, ports, consoles, removable media or engineering equipment.
Assessment Focus: Assess physical zones, badges, visitor controls, cabinet/console security and media controls.
Safety Mode: No bypass of live safety/security controls without explicit authorization.
Expected Evidence: Access logs, photographs where allowed, physical control evidence.
Potential Impact: Direct device compromise or safety risk.

Description: BMS/HVAC/CCTV/access control networks can provide an unintended enterprise foothold if poorly segmented.
Assessment Focus: Review segmentation, default credentials, remote access, vendor support and monitoring.
Expected Evidence: Network diagrams, ACLs, system configs, vendor access records.

Description: Compromise of power, water, HVAC, compressed air, steam or cooling controls can affect manufacturing availability/safety.
Assessment Focus: Assess utility dependencies, segmentation, access control, monitoring and manual fallback.
Safety Mode: No manipulation of live utility controls.
Expected Evidence: Dependency maps, access controls, logs, contingency evidence.

Attack Path: Monitoring blind spot to attacker activity
Description: Missing telemetry or weak detection can allow attacker activity to persist or evade response.
Assessment Focus: Assess log coverage, OT telemetry, time sync, detection use cases, alert routing and retention.
Safety Mode: Read-only validation and approved test events.
Expected Evidence: Log samples, detection rules, alert evidence, time synchronization.

Description: Identity, PKI or time-service weaknesses can undermine authentication and event correlation.
Assessment Focus: Assess certificate trust, key protection, NTP/PTP architecture, identity dependencies and monitoring.
Expected Evidence: PKI configs, certificate inventory, time-source evidence, logs.
Potential Impact: Authentication bypass or forensic blind spots.

Description: Compromise or manipulation of AI pipelines, data, models, APIs or model-serving infrastructure can affect decisions or expose sensitive data.
Assessment Focus: Assess model/data access, pipeline identity, input validation, provenance, secrets, API authorization and monitoring.
Safety Mode: No unsafe model-driven actuation tests in production.
Expected Evidence: Model/data lineage, API logs, IAM, deployment evidence.
Potential Impact: Incorrect predictions, IP/data exposure, operational decisions affected.

Description: Designs, drawings, source code, BOMs, recipes and project files may be collected after repository compromise.
Assessment Focus: Assess repository permissions, segmentation, encryption, DLP, monitoring and retention.
Expected Evidence: Access logs, permissions, sample evidence, DLP alerts.

Description: Rugged tablets, barcode/RFID terminals and mobile apps can provide access to operational workflows.
Assessment Focus: Review device management, app controls, identity, wireless segmentation and data storage.
Expected Evidence: MDM policy, app config, auth logs, network evidence.

Typical Path: Remote Access & Third Parties / Supply Chain → Enterprise/OT
Description: Vendor software, drivers, packages, updates and support channels may introduce compromise.
Assessment Focus: Assess vendor assurance, signatures, provenance, SBOM, change approvals and monitoring.
Expected Evidence: Vendor attestations, hashes/signatures, SBOM, change records.

Description: Protocol gateways, ESB, brokers, ETL and integration middleware can bridge trust zones.
Tactic Sequence: Discovery → Lateral Movement → C2 → Process Control
Assessment Focus: Assess interface authorization, protocol translation, allowlists, queues, certificates and logging.
Expected Evidence: Gateway config, ACLs, message logs, certificates.

Description: Compromised backup/project/image restored to production can reintroduce malicious or unsafe state.
Assessment Focus: Assess golden-image provenance, backup integrity, restore validation, offline copies and change approval.
Safety Mode: Validate in isolated recovery/lab where possible.
Expected Evidence: Hashes, restore logs, golden image records, approvals.

Typical Path: Industrial Networks / Cloud / Remote Access → Multiple Plants
Description: WAN, SD-WAN, site-to-site VPN or shared services can create paths between plants.
Assessment Focus: Assess site isolation, routing, firewall policy, shared identity and monitoring.
Expected Evidence: WAN topology, ACLs, routes, flow logs.

Description: Compromise of QMS/LIMS/traceability/serialization data can create quality, compliance or recall risks without directly changing a PLC.
Assessment Focus: Assess integrity, authorization, audit trails, segregation and reconciliation.
Expected Evidence: Transaction/audit logs, role matrices, integrity checks.

Description: WMS, scanners, AGVs, ASRS and logistics integrations can affect material flow and production continuity.
Assessment Focus: Assess wireless/app/API controls, device identity, segmentation and recovery.
Expected Evidence: Workflow logs, device inventory, API evidence.
Potential Impact: Material flow interruption and production delay.

Description: Temporary laptops, engineering tools or portable media may bridge trusted and untrusted environments.
Assessment Focus: Assess onboarding, endpoint posture, isolation, media controls and teardown.
Expected Evidence: Asset check-in/out, posture evidence, access logs.
Potential Impact: Unauthorized entry into OT or data exposure.
